cohort: 10,408 mothers with children under 12 months old in 12 regions of China
finding: The prevalence of breastfeeding in 12 selected regions in China was low, with exclusive breastfeeding rates decreasing from 32.71% at ages 0-3 months to 15.83% at ages 3-5 months, and several factors including cesarean section, higher income, maternal education, and employment status were associated with lower breastfeeding rates.
mod_finding: Cesarean section had a negative association with early breastfeeding initiation, exclusive breastfeeding, and predominant breastfeeding.
